title: Embedding-Driven Construction of Internal Metal−Semiconductor−Semiconductor Heterostructures within Single Crystals
abstract: Constructing heterostructures within single crystals remains a fundamental challenge in materials synthesis, as most approaches rely on post-synthetic assembly that limits interfacial integration and structural coherence. Here we report an occlusion strategy that enables the embedding of preformed nanoparticle building blocks to encode internal metal−semiconductor−semiconductor heterostructures within a model semiconductor matrix. Platinum-loaded metal−organic framework nanoparticles are incorporated during the crystallization of silver phosphate, yielding composites with spatially confined and intimately integrated internal interfaces. This embedding process establishes a structural basis for directional charge transport, in which photogenerated electrons are preferentially extracted towards the embedded metal sites while holes are retained within the host lattice. As a result, the composite exhibits suppressed photocorrosion and enhanced oxidative reactivity, achieving efficient oxygen evolution together with sustained operational stability. More broadly, this work demonstrates that nanoparticle embedding during crystal growth provides a generalizable route to engineer internal heterostructures, offering a potential paradigm for controlling charge migration through structure-encoded design.

title: Coordination‐Driven Spiral Self‐Assembly of Helical Mesoporous Polymer Nanospheres and Derived MoS 2 /Carbon Colloidal Nanospheres for Fast Lithium Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Helical mesoporous architectures are attractive for electrochemical energy storage because their curved channels and spiral surfaces facilitate ion transport and interfacial charge transfer. However, their synthesis has traditionally relied on chiral templates or complex assembly procedures, limiting structural tunability and compositional flexibility. Herein, we develop a coordination‐driven spiral self‐assembly (CSS) strategy that converts achiral building blocks into helical mesoporous polymer nanospheres (HMPSs) with continuous spiral surface textures and internal helical mesopores. Interfacial Mo–S coordination drives micellar spiral organization without chiral additives, enabling systematic regulation of pore size, morphology, and composition. Subsequent carbonization transforms HMPSs into helical mesoporous MoS 2 /C nanospheres (HMMoS 2 /C) containing uniformly dispersed monolayer MoS 2 while retaining the helical mesostructure. Finite‐element simulations and density functional theory calculations reveal that the helical mesoporous architecture facilitates rapid Li + diffusion, local ion enrichment, and interfacial charge transfer, thereby improving Li‐storage kinetics. Consequently, HMMoS 2 /C delivers a reversible capacity of 1776.3 mAh g − 1 at 0.3 A g − 1 after 150 cycles, a high‐rate capacity of 752.7 mAh g − 1 at 10 A g − 1 , and outstanding long‐term cycling stability. This work establishes coordination‐driven self‐assembly as a versatile route to helical mesoporous materials for energy storage.

title: Interfacial molecular gateway via supramolecular assembly on metal–organic framework for highly selective CO 2 separation
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive CO 2 separation from industrial gas offers an energy‐efficient approach for carbon capture, but is restricted by simultaneously achieving high adsorption capacity and selectivity. Herein, we report an interfacial molecular gateway engineering strategy on metal–organic framework that enhances selective CO 2 transport while preserving intrinsic framework porosity. A supramolecular assembly approach was developed to construct a robust imidazolium polymer shell on mesoporous MIL‐101(Cr) through supramolecular interactions, circumventing pore‐blocking limitations commonly encountered in core–shell architectures. Benefiting from synergy between electrostatic and hydrogen‐bonding attractions in the shell and efficient molecular transport in the core, the heterostructure exhibits IAST selectivities of 1029 for CO 2 /N 2 and 97 for CO 2 /CH 4 , while nearly doubling the CO 2 adsorption capacity of MIL‐101(Cr). This enables direct production of high‐purity CO 2 (>99 vol.%) from simulated flue gas and natural gas. This work establishes a versatile interfacial engineering platform for porous frameworks, providing a promising route toward high‐performance adsorbents for industrial gas purification.

title: Linker Conjugation Engineering of Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis in Neutral Media
abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising molecularly versatile electrocatalysts for H 2 O 2 production through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR). Most COF‐based catalysts operate in alkaline media, which results in rapid H 2 O 2 decomposition and limits product accumulation. Thus, developing catalytic COFs for efficient neutral H 2 O 2 systems remains highly challenging. Herein, two tetraphenylethylene (TPE)‐based COFs (TPE‐EDA‐COF and TPE‐ADA‐COF) have been constructed to catalyze 2e − ORR in neutral media. The conjugated degree of COFs was modulated by inserting C─C and C≡C bonds in the linkers. By introducing the C≡C bond in the linker, TPE‐ADA‐COF showed enhanced π‐conjugation, narrowed the optical bandgap, and facilitated charge transport. The TPE‐ADA‐COF exhibited an H 2 O 2 selectivity of 86.0% and a mass activity of 26.83 A g −1 at a potential of 0.01 V versus RHE, while TPE‐EDA‐COF showed lower selectivity of 80.9% and mass activity of 25.67 A g −1. At 180 mA cm −2, the flow cell delivered an H 2 O 2 productivity of approximately 4920 mmol g −1 h −1. In a separate stability test conducted at 20 mA cm −2, the flow cell operated continuously for 60 h with an average Faradaic efficiency of approximately 87%. These results establish linker‐conjugation engineering as an effective strategy for neutral H 2 O 2 electrosynthesis using metal‐free COFs.

title: Hierarchically Porous Metal–Organic Frameworks as Multifunctional Platforms for Synergistic Chemo-Photo-Biocatalytic Enantioselective Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer a promising platform for the precise customization of multifunctional composites, enabling the optimization of synergistic effects between catalysts and significantly enhancing both stability and catalytic performance. Despite this potential, this idealized system is still in the exploratory stage. Herein, we integrated a chemical catalyst with a photoenzyme-based enantioselective catalytic platform into a single system, achieving the sequential transformation from C2-alkylation to asymmetric Mannich reaction products. A hierarchically porous (HP) UiO-67 material was constructed as the supporting platform. Through a post-synthetic ligand exchange strategy, Pd(II) and Ru(II) catalysts were simultaneously immobilized, while wheat germ lipase (WGL) was encapsulated within the mesoporous channels, yielding the multifunctional catalyst WGL@HP-UiO-67-Pd/Ru. This catalyst afforded satisfactory yields of 62–94% in the C2-arylation reaction and enantioselectivities of 69–93% in the asymmetric Mannich reaction. In this sequential catalytic transformation, the multifunctional catalyst afforded an overall efficiency of 47.6%, corresponding to a 3.8-fold enhancement over the homogeneous catalyst system. These findings provide deeper insight into the role of multifunctional catalysis in sequential reactions and underscore its considerable promise for the asymmetric synthesis of organic compounds and pharmaceutical agents.

title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
abstract: Band-filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid-band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π-conjugated electron-donating molecules are covalently linked to form one-dimensional pore channels. The introduction of a well-defined amount of electron-accepting molecules without disrupting the framework structure enabled the first successful demonstration of the deliberate band-filling control while elucidating the charge state through various spectroscopic measurements. Enhanced electronic itinerancy facilitated by host-guest charge transfer was evidenced by spectroscopic, transport, and magnetic measurements in support of theoretical calculations. The present study opens a new avenue for exploring more advanced electronic organic solids based on band-filling engineering.

title: Tuning Fatty Acid-Templated Mesoporous Silica for Adsorption and Hemocompatibility
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous silica was synthesized via a green sol–gel route using biosourced C16–C18 fatty acid mixtures as structure-directing agents. Tuning the silica precursor, solvent, and pH allowed precise control over the interfacial self-assembly, shifting the template state from encapsulated free fatty acids (acidic) to saponified soap micelles (basic). The optimized fumed silica/NaOH sample (ST4) exhibited exceptional textural properties, featuring a high surface area (958 m²·g⁻¹), large pore volume (0.89 cm³·g⁻¹), and a predominantly mesoporous character (79%) with a highly ordered hexagonal structure. This tailored architecture enabled efficient, balanced adsorption of small blood biomolecules (urea, creatinine, and glucose) while demonstrating excellent hemocompatibility (< 3% hemolysis, ISO 10993-4). These findings highlight the potential of eco-friendly, fatty acid-templated mesoporous silica as a highly effective and biocompatible platform for blood purification and biomedical applications.

title: Ytterbium Metal‐Organic Framework With DNA Hydrogel Switching for ElectroChemiluminescence Biosensing
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensors typically rely on stepwise assembly of recognition probes and signal labels directly on electrode surfaces, which suffers from severe fouling and poor reproducibility when dealing with crude plant extracts. Here, we discover that a pre‐reduction treatment at −3 V boosts the cathodic ECL of an ytterbium metal‐organic framework (Yb‐MOF) by 14‐fold through a radical‐accumulation mechanism. Leveraging this emitter, we construct a spatially decoupled biosensor that physically separates target recognition from signal transduction using a DNA hydrogel. In a test tube, CRISPR‐Cas12a activated by the Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus outer membrane protein ( C Las Omp) gene cleaves a rolling circle amplification derived DNA hydrogel, releasing encapsulated Fe 3 O 4 nanolabels. After magnetic separation, these labels are simply dropped onto the Yb‐MOF electrode, inducing ECL quenching via resonance energy transfer (RET). The ECL change (ΔECL) exhibits a linear relationship with the target concentration over the range of 10 pM to 100 nM, affording a detection limit of 2 pM. Moreover, the sensor demonstrates single‐base mismatch discrimination. The spatial decoupling strategy provides a robust paradigm for plant pathogen surveillance in complex agricultural matrices.

title: Superoxide Dismutase‐Functionalized Titanium Dioxide Colloidosomes for Enhanced UV Protection and Persistent ROS Suppression
abstract: Titanium dioxide (TiO 2), serving as a prominent inorganic ultraviolet (UV) filter, has been widely utilized in photoprotective formulations. However, its photocatalytic activity under UV irradiation generates reactive oxygen species (ROS), thereby raising significant concerns regarding photochemical safety. Although antioxidant coatings have been proposed to suppress TiO 2 ‐induced ROS, persistent ROS suppression remains challenging due to the intrinsically sacrificial nature of conventional antioxidant components. Herein, we report an efficient strategy for constructing superoxide dismutase (SOD)‐functionalized TiO 2 colloidosomes (STCs) for persistent ROS suppression. SOD is first electrostatically adsorbed onto TiO 2 nanoparticles, followed by droplet‐confined self‐assembly of the resulting SOD–TiO 2 nanoparticles into hollow mesoporous colloidosomes. This hierarchical design enables in situ scavenging of photogenerated ROS at the TiO 2 interface while stabilizing SOD. Compared with bare TiO 2 NPs, the STCs exhibit an approximately 1.81‐fold enhancement in Sun Protection Factor (SPF). Moreover, the STCs maintain ROS inhibition efficiencies above 95% over three consecutive 6 h UV irradiation cycles and exhibit low cytotoxicity in the tested HaCaT cells. This study provides a feasible strategy for the development of TiO 2 ‐based UV filtration materials that integrate enhanced UV protection with persistent enzymatic antioxidant functionality, highlighting their potential applications in advanced photoprotective materials and sunscreen formulations for human health.

title: Intermetallic‐Reinforced Yolk–Shell Architecture for Long‐Life, High‐Rate Silicon Anodes
abstract: Managing Si expansion without sacrificing charge transport remains a key challenge in high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries. In this study, lepidocrocite‐type titanate and graphene oxide nanosheets are used as reactive, spatially programmed precursors to construct a yolk–shell composite comprising a porous Si/SiO x yolk confined within a Ti 5 Si 3 –reduced graphene oxide (rGO) shell (PSiO@TSG‐YS). Layer‐by‐layer assembly, controlled core etching, and magnesiothermic conversion collectively create an internal expansion reservoir, a mechanically reinforcing Ti 5 Si 3 framework, and an electronically percolating rGO network. Microscopy, diffraction, Ti K‐edge X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, and solid‐state 29 Si magic‐angle‐spinning nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy verify Ti 5 Si 3 formation and Ti–Si coordination. The resulting architecture limits electrode swelling to 10.9% after 100 cycles and maintains low polarization and diffusion impedance during prolonged cycling. PSiO@TSG‐YS retains 70.5% of its second‐cycle capacity after 3500 cycles at 0.5 A g −1. An NCM811||PSiO@TSG‐YS full cell retains 86.1% of its initial capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C. Reactive nanosheet‐to‐intermetallic conversion thus integrates geometric buffering, interfacial stabilization, and electronic percolation in high‐capacity alloying electrodes.

title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
abstract: Abstract Heterochromatin typically represses genes 1,2 , yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation 3–7 . How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent 8 . In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly 8 . By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
abstract: Abstract CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex 1,2 . Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools 3–6 . Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST ( Pse CAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far 7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution 8 . However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation 9 . Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the Pse CAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the Pse CAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa Pse CAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

title: Chiral Bobbers in the Room‐Temperature Magnet Co 8 Zn 10 Mn 2
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral bobbers are three‐dimensional magnetic solitons that emerge near surfaces of chiral magnets with bulk‐type Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. They can be regarded as skyrmion strings terminated by a Bloch point inside the material. So far, chiral bobbers have been observed only at cryogenic temperatures. Here, we report the direct observation of chiral bobbers in over a broad temperature range, including room temperature. Using Lorentz transmission electron microscopy combined with micromagnetic simulations, we identify a previously unreported nucleation pathway in which skyrmion strings transform into chiral bobbers under an applied magnetic field. We also demonstrate that chiral bobbers on opposite surfaces can be coupled to form double‐bobber states. These findings establish chiral bobbers as room‐temperature magnetic textures and identify their role in the nucleation pathways of topological magnetic solitons.

title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
abstract: ABSTRACT One‐step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl‐orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket‐site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs + , Sr 2+ and UO 2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl‐orchestrated enol‐imine to keto‐enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone‐carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO 2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO2 2+ uptake of 336 mg g −1 and a Cs + permeation flux of 0.26 mol m −2 h −1 , while exhibiting suppressed Sr 2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs + /Sr 2+ and Cs + /UO 2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl‐orchestrated crystallization and pocket‐site engineering as a powerful approach for multi‐component ion separations.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

title: Halogenated Triazole-Based Metal–Organic Framework Achieves Ultra-Selective CO2 Capture under Humid Conditions
abstract: Abstract Selective CO2 capture from humid, N2-rich flue gas requires adsorbents that combine extreme CO2/N2 discrimination with robustness under realistic conditions. However, only a few MOFs are able to combine ultrahigh selectivity, humidity tolerance, scalable synthesis, and structural durability. Here, we introduce CALF-20-X (X = Cl or Br) halogentriazolate–oxalate Zn-MOFs and a PVDF composite, integrating these attributes into an ultramicroporous framework. The halogenated Zn-MOFs are obtained by means of solvent-minimized liquid-assisted grinding followed by water-incubation route, producing a highly crystalline material. Halogen functionalization polarizes the triazolate C–H donor, thereby promoting directional C–H···O(CO2) contacts and enhancing electrostatic complementarity, as evidenced by an experimental isosteric heat of adsorption of 48 kJ/mol. Furthermore, this halogen substitution significantly restricts the size of the pore window inhibiting N2 uptake, and leads to the formation of perfectly CO2-fitted pockets. These combined features enabled a CO2 excellent adsorption of 2.89 mmol g–1 at 0.15 bar and 298 K, and CO2/N2 selectivity higher than 4074 for CALF-20-Cl, exceeding leading physisorbent benchmarks. The highly selective CO2 capture was confirmed by dynamic breakthrough experiments performed on a CALF-20-Cl@PVDF composite under humid conditions over numerous cycles, thus demonstrating its robust performance under flue-gas-relevant conditions. Competitive CO2/H2O breakthrough experiments, supported by GCMC simulations, demonstrate that CO2 sorption is favored at 21% relative humidity (RH), resulting in a 56% suppression of water uptake, and even remains competitive at RH &gt; 50% and 318 K, a temperature relevant for carbon capture from point sources. These results highlight halogen-driven structural engineering for regenerable and humidity-tolerant next-generation CO2-selective MOF adsorbents with complete retention of the performance metrics.

title: Thermodynamic–Kinetic Synergy Enables Neon/Helium Separation in an Anion‐Pillared Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: ABSTRACT Separating neon (Ne) from helium (He) remains challenging because both gases are chemically inert and weakly interacting, while classical size‐sieving principles predict faster transport for the smaller He atom. Here we address this challenge with the anion‐pillared metal–organic framework (MOF) Ni(4‐DPDS) 2 CrO 4 , whose confined pores combine narrow apertures with electrostatically heterogeneous cavities. This environment provides multiple weak contacts that favor Ne adsorption while producing an inverse diffusional response relative to the expected size trend. At 77 K and 100 kPa, the framework adsorbs 50.63 cm 3 g −1 of Ne but only 0.40 cm 3 g −1 of He in static adsorption, with a kinetic Ne/He selectivity of 113.58. Fixed‐bed experiments afford He with a purity above 99.999%, followed by temperature‐driven recovery of Ne with a purity above 99.7%. The results show that coordinating adsorption thermodynamics with molecular transport offers a route to separating weakly interacting gases beyond equilibrium affinity or classical size sieving alone.

title: Chiral Porous Silica for Enantioselective Separation: From Molecular Recognition to Chiral Architectures
abstract: Chiral recognition is the basis for all enantioselective separation techniques by enabling differential interactions between enantiomers and chiral environments. Although classical enantioseparation has relied primarily on molecular-chiral selectors, recent advances have extended these principles to architecturally engineered porous materials. This mini-review discusses the evolution of chiral mesoporous silica for enantioselective separation, emphasizing the relationship between molecular recognition and materials design. We first summarize the thermodynamic basis of chiral recognition, highlighting the pioneering mechanistic contributions of Prof. Bezhan Chankvetadze, who established that enantioselectivity arises from differences in the stability of transient diastereomeric host-guest complexes. We then review the development of chiral porous silica, from molecular imprinting and structurally chiral silica architectures to functionally chiral mesoporous materials and hierarchical chiral colloidosomes capable of enantioselective adsorption and separation. We next discuss current understanding of the underlying recognition mechanisms, including chirality transfer during synthesis, geometric confinement, cooperative host-guest interactions, and adsorption thermodynamics. Finally, we highlight emerging opportunities involving chiral metal-organic frameworks, chiral covalent organic frameworks, atomic layer deposition, and related hybrid porous systems. The convergence of molecular recognition and rational materials engineering provides a foundation for the next generation of porous materials for enantioselective separation, adsorption, asymmetric catalysis, and chiral sensing.

title: Self-Assembly–Galvanic Replacement Route to Conformal Ag Nanoflower Interfaces for Dendrite-Suppressed Zn Anodes
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable aqueous Zn anodes are severely limited by sluggish interfacial kinetics and morphological instability. Herein, we report a simple and vacuum-free self-assembly/galvanic replacement strategy that converts a silver nanoplate dispersion into a conformal Ag nanoflower scaffold on Zn foil (Zn@AgNF). This porous and highly wetting metallic interface provides continuous electron-transport pathways and a favorable interfacial environment for Zn nucleation, thereby promoting more uniform Zn deposition and improved interfacial kinetics. Ex situ morphological observations suggest a progressive deposition evolution toward compact Zn deposits with reduced surface oxidation. Symmetric cells exhibit reduced nucleation and growth overpotentials, narrow voltage hysteresis across a wide current-density range, and stable cycling at 10 mA cm–2. In rechargeable Zn–air full cells, Zn@AgNF decreases round-trip polarization and stabilizes interfacial impedance, while improving the full-cell Coulombic efficiency and cycling endurance under the tested conditions (5 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2). These advantages are maintained in gel electrolytes, in which the cells tolerate repeated bending up to 180°. This work demonstrates a simple solution-based interfacial engineering strategy for improving Zn deposition stability in aqueous Zn-based energy-storage systems.

title: Reticular Chemistry: A Systematic Approach to the Design and Discovery of Novel Metal-Organic Framework
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are a class of crystalline porous materials whose structures can be rationally assembled from metal clusters and organic linkers into predetermined topologies, offering precise control over pore size, connectivity, and function. Despite this design potential, the strong thermodynamic preference for a limited set of default topologies means that most predicted MOF structures remain synthetically inaccessible, restricting the structural diversity available to reticular chemistry. This dissertation addresses this challenge by developing topological design principles and validating them through targeted synthesis across distinct MOF platforms. The work begins by extending net expansion and face decoration, established topological operations, to 28 parent nets, generating 24 new cage-containing topologies spanning tetrahedral, cubic, trigonal-prismatic, and octahedral cage geometries. A torsion angle parameter is introduced as a predictive design criterion, where topologies with torsion angles of 0° or 60° correspond to geometrically ideal, synthetically accessible node environments, while intermediate values identify targets that are more synthetically demanding. Among the topologies identified, hmc, flu-e, and dcw are selected for experimental realization. The hmc and flu-e targets are realized using the centring structure-directing agent (cSDA) strategy, in which nitrogen-donor ligands template specific windows to direct assembly toward the intended cage geometry. Five isoreticular hmc-MOFs and one flu-e MOF are synthesized, each incorporating three distinct, well-defined cage types. Control experiments confirm that the cSDA directs framework assembly rather than merely occupying pore space, and a geometric design equation relating ligand and cSDA length is shown to correctly predict all five hmc combinations prior to synthesis. This design logic is then extended to the previously unreported xaw net and its derivatives, daw and dcw, targeted through the combination of a tetratopic linker, a bent ditopic linker, and the In₃O oxotrimer. Initial synthesis in the absence of a cSDA yields only a competing polymorph; introducing TPPP as a flexible cSDA demonstrates that selectivity, rather than size compatibility alone, governs which topology forms. Net clipping of the resulting Indcw-MOF-413 further generates the pcp-t framework, though both new frameworks exhibit limited porosity upon activation, identifying framework stability as a remaining challenge. The final part of this dissertation shifts to a distinct inorganic platform, holding the NiNbOF₅ pillar of the benchmark CO₂ sorbent KAUST-7 constant while systematically varying the organic ligand across six linkers of different geometry and connectivity. Unlike the pillar, the ligand is found to exert no predictable control over the resulting topology or porosity: two isoreticular frameworks differing by only two nitrogen atoms diverge completely in gas uptake, and one, NbOFFIVE-PYRM-Ni, exhibits reversible, CO₂-triggered gate-opening behavior not observed elsewhere in the series, tentatively attributed to its uncoordinated pyrimidine nitrogen atoms.

title: The Chemistry and Applications of High-Connectivity Metal–Organic Frameworks: From Carboxylate-Based to Benzotriazolate-Based Platforms
abstract: Conspectus Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), assembled from inorganic nodes and organic linkers via strong coordination bonds, are functional crystalline porous materials. Reticular chemistry can guide the assembly of targeted MOFs from preselected building blocks encoding the geometrical information on underlying networks. Among them, high-connectivity nets are important for the designed synthesis of high-connectivity MOF materials, assembled from associated building blocks, thanks to their high structural predictability. These building blocks can be polytopic organic ligands, polynuclear clusters and metal–organic polyhedra, and their geometrical shapes and connectivities often precisely match the targeted high-connectivity nets. High-connectivity carboxylate-based MOFs often display high porosity and are promising adsorbents for gases while benzotriazolate-based MOFs are emerging as a distinctive subclass of MOFs constructed by robust metal–nitrogen bonds, which can stabilize reactive species such as low-valent metal centers, therefore enhancing guest-framework interactions. To this end, it remains a challenge to rationally assemble high-connectivity building blocks into carboxylate- and benzotriazolate-based MOFs with tailored pore structures and functionalities for advanced applications. In this Account, we summarized recent progress from our group toward the synthesis and applications of high-connectivity MOFs, ranging from carboxylate-based to benzotriazolate-based platforms. We first introduced π-extended PrismCage building units into isoreticular (6,6)-connected nia-MOFs for enhanced supramolecular host–guest interactions. Next, we established a net-coded organic building block strategy to rationally construct (4,12)-connected shp-MOFs and (6,12)-connected alb-MOFs via the assembly of a 12-connected hexagonal-prismatic dodecacarboxylate ligand and geometrically different inorganic nodes. Next, we further developed a heterosupermolecular-building-block approach to assemble trinodal (3,12,24)-connected uru-MOFs by assembling 12-connected cuboctahedral and 24-connected rhombicuboctahedral metal–organic polyhedra, which are linked by 3-connected organic units. The high-porosity uru-MOF-1 exhibits good low-temperature methane storage performances. We also applied a multicomponent merged-net strategy to precisely synthesize (3,6,9)-connected tsn-MOF-1 by assembling 9-connected metal-containing trinuclear clusters, 6-connected triptycene-based carboxylates, and 3-connected pyridine-based linkers. The robust tsn-MOF-1 can facilely be activated from common solvents to achieve full porosity, exhibiting good methane and hydrogen storage performances. Apart from carboxylate-based MOF platforms, we constructed functional benzotriazolate-based MOFs using multitopic benzotriazolate ligands synthesized via sequential reactions including general Suzuki coupling reactions. We first synthesized a tritopic benzotriazolate ligand and assembled it with copper ions to form a rod-packing MOF with high ionic conductivity. Furthermore, the assembly of a hexatopic benzotriazolate ligand and Zn5 clusters forms a (6,6)-connected nia-MOF, Zn-Tz6Mes. The isostructural CuI-Zn-Tz6Mes with open Cu(I) sites exhibits enhanced binding affinities toward π-acidic gases such as H2 and N2 compared to the parent Zn-Tz6Mes. The serendipitous assembly of a tritopic tris-benzotriazolate ligand and zinc ions afford a (3,6,6)-connected pco-MOF, Zn-TBTB, displaying a complex cage-within-cage structure and modular anionic pore environments for high Li+ conductivity. Finally, we give a brief perspective toward high-connectivity functional MOFs and hope this Account can serve as a guiding blueprint for the development of next-generation high-connectivity MOFs with embedded functionalities, thereby advancing the field of the solid-state materials in general.

title: Synergistic Water‐Deficient Inner Helmholtz Plane and Asymmetric Dual‐Site Nonmetal Catalysts Enable Stable Ah‐Level Aqueous Zn–I 2 Batteries at Elevated Temperatures
abstract: ABSTRACT At elevated temperatures, intensified water‐induced side reactions and iodine dissolution severely hinder the development of aqueous zinc–iodine batteries. Herein, a marginally hydrophilic and conductive modification layer with a hexagonal layered structure is constructed to stabilize the anode interface. This approach establishes a water‐deficient inner Helmholtz plane and reduces the fraction of weak hydrogen bonds, thereby suppressing spontaneous Zn dissolution and water decomposition. Concurrently, interfacial electronic structure regulation increases the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction and promotes uniform Zn deposition along the Zn‐(002) crystal plane, effectively inhibiting dendrite growth. These effects are corroborated by theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations. Furthermore, asymmetric dual‐site nonmetal single‐atom–cluster structures are introduced into the cathode host to enhance iodine adsorption and accelerate conversion kinetics, thereby mitigating iodine dissolution. Benefiting from this synergistic design, the assembled coin‐type battery delivers a discharge capacity of 95 mAh g −1 after 60 000 cycles at 8 A g −1 . A sub‐ampere‐hour‐level plastic‐cased battery employing a high‐loading cathode with a theoretical areal‐capacity of 5.6 mAh cm −2 further demonstrates strong practical potential by maintaining excellent cycling stability at 3 C and at 50°C. An Ah‐level pouch battery also exhibits stable operation at 50°C.

title: Reconstructing Structural Dynamic Cooperativity Suppresses Conduction Loss in Linear Aliphatic Polymer Dielectrics at Elevated Temperatures
abstract: ABSTRACT Linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics show increased conduction loss at elevated temperatures as thermally activated structural fluctuations modulate electronic states and facilitate charge transport. We examine how aromatic side groups with different π‐electron delocalization affect structural dynamic cooperativity and charge transport. Side‐group modification alters intermolecular interactions and local dynamic constraints, shifting long‐range cooperative motion to localized heterogeneous fluctuations. This transition coincides with reduced collective structural fluctuations and improved local electronic‐state stability, consistent with suppressed phonon‐assisted carrier transport. As a result, the furan‐modified polymer exhibits a statistical electronic energy fluctuation descriptor of 0.132 eV and nearly two orders of magnitude higher volume resistivity. It achieves a discharged energy density of 8.38 J cm −3 at 120°C, approximately 45 times that of pristine polymer while maintaining a charge‐discharge efficiency above 90%. It also retains an efficiency above 93% over 5 × 10 5 charge‐discharge cycles at 200 MV m −1 . Although the higher glass transition temperature of the furan‐modified polymer may also contribute to its performance near 120°C, its advantage is already evident at 25°C and 80°C, well below the glass‐transition regime. This work highlights structural dynamic cooperativity as a descriptor linking molecular dynamics and charge transport in linear aliphatic polymer dielectrics.

title: Data‐Driven Conformational Mismatch Design Enables Extreme‐Temperature Energy Storage in Copolyimides
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐temperature capacitive energy storage requires polymer dielectrics to combine a wide optical bandgap ( E g ) with a high glass‐transition temperature ( T g ), properties that are often difficult to optimize simultaneously through conventional backbone design. Here, we introduce conformational mismatch into semi‐alicyclic polyimide copolymers and identify promising monomer combinations through a multistage workflow integrating machine‐learning prediction of T g , density‐functional‐theory calculations of electronic structure, and molecular‐dynamics analysis of chain conformations. Incorporating a methyl‐substituted diamine yields Co‐PI‐tC, in which local conformational mismatch modifies molecular fluctuations and chain packing while suppressing thermally activated charge transport. Conformational entropy estimates derived from atomic fluctuations quantitatively capture these changes and complement conventional structural and electronic descriptors. The resulting Co‐PI‐tC film combines a T g of 271.52°C with E g of 4.28 eV, delivers a discharged energy density of 8.6 J cm −3 at 200°C with 90% efficiency and retains 6.7 J cm −3 at 250°C, setting a high‐temperature energy‐storage record among reported copolymer dielectrics. These results establish conformational mismatch as an effective molecular‐design strategy for reconciling thermal stability and electrical insulation in high‐temperature polymer dielectrics.

title: Programming PEDOT:PSS Architecture and Gelation via Binary Eutectic Liquid–Driven Interfacial Assembly
abstract: ABSTRACT Water‐soluble electrolytes, including ionic liquids, promote PEDOT:PSS gelation by screening interparticle electrostatic repulsions, necessitating precise tuning of ionic strength in homogeneous aqueous systems. Timed electrolyte release in aqueous systems is therefore essential for directing gel formation into designed architecture and enhancing its electrical properties, yet effective strategies remain limited. This work introduces a previously unreported liquid–liquid interfacial assembly platform based on binary hydrophobic eutectic liquids (HEL), in which interfacial PEDOT:PSS–HEL complexation directs aqueous‐phase morphology and triggers subsequent gelation of PEDOT:PSS. By varying the hydrogen‐bond acceptor while maintaining a constant hydrogen‐bond donor, the ionic character of the HEL is tuned to regulate interfacial assembly. Simultaneously, hydrogen‐bonding interactions within the HEL limit electrolyte migration into the aqueous phase, thereby triggering PEDOT:PSS gelation while suppressing phase separation associated with rapid electrolyte release. This controlled interfacial process suppresses Rayleigh–Plateau instabilities and enables depth‐propagating gelation throughout the aqueous bulk, providing a versatile route to architected, high‐performance PEDOT:PSS gels, including chemically programmed liquid‐to‐gel temporal devices.

title: Corona-Length Dependence of Equilibrium Fusion and Fragmentation Energy Barriers in Block Copolymer Micelles
abstract: Abstract Fusion and fragmentation are intrinsic dynamic pathways in block copolymer micelles, governing both structural transformations and the transport of solubilized molecules. Yet, how the macromolecular architecture controls their energetic barriers remains poorly understood. In particular, while the influence of the core-forming block has been investigated, the contribution of the corona remains less explored, especially for fusion under equilibrium conditions. Here, this contribution is examined by quantifying equilibrium fusion and fragmentation kinetics in aqueous Pluronic PEO–PPO–PEO micelles from the time-resolved intermicellar exchange of an extremely hydrophobic fluorescent probe. A systematic series of copolymers with comparable PPO block lengths and PEO blocks spanning approximately 17–140 EO units was examined in the spherical-micelle regime and combined with previously reported data for copolymers spanning a broader range of PPO block lengths. Increasing the corona length produces only weak changes in both fusion and fragmentation rates, in marked contrast to the much stronger dependence on core length. The apparent activation energies for fusion and fragmentation are remarkably similar in magnitude and exhibit closely related dependences on block architecture. For both processes, this dependence is described by a common scaling form, ΔEapp ∝ NcoreaNcoronab, with a ≈ 1.3–2 and b close to zero. These results demonstrate that the energetic cost of equilibrium fusion and fragmentation is governed predominantly by the micellar core.

title: Antimetastatic Sulfonate-Functionalized Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles Enhance Irinotecan Stability and Delivery for Colorectal Cancer Treatment
abstract: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with irinotecan (IRI) serving as a backbone chemotherapeutic despite its dose-limiting toxicities, instability of the active lactone form, and lack of intrinsic antimetastatic activity. To overcome these barriers, we developed sulfonate-functionalized mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs), referred to as (SO3-)-MSN-PEG/TA, as a multifunctional nanocarrier for IRI delivery. This nanoformulation markedly enhanced drug loading efficiency and preserved over 90% of IRI in its lactone form for up to six months, enabling sustained release and improved pharmacological stability. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient nanoparticle internalization, while IRI@(SO3-)-MSN-PEG/TA enhanced apoptosis and reduced the IC50 compared with free IRI. Beyond drug delivery, (SO3-)-MSN-PEG/TA exhibited intrinsic antimetastatic activity associated with modulation of focal adhesion kinase/paxillin signaling and impaired tumor cell adhesion and migration. The nanoparticles also exhibited efficient tumor accumulation through the enhanced permeability and retention effect. Pharmacokinetic analysis further revealed that IRI@(SO3-)-MSN-PEG/TA prolonged systemic retention, maintaining approximately threefold higher IRI plasma concentrations than free IRI. IRI@(SO3-)-MSN-PEG/TA significantly inhibited both primary tumor growth and metastatic dissemination in orthotopic and heterotopic colorectal cancer models, while markedly reducing systemic toxicities and preserving bone marrow cellularity relative to free IRI and liposomal IRI (Onivyde). Transcriptomic profiling further revealed attenuation of extracellular matrix/mesenchymal remodeling and hypoxia/vascular-associated programs, providing molecular support for the observed antimetastatic phenotype. Consistently, reduced vascular endothelial growth factor expression and tumor-associated angiogenesis were observed in the chorioallantoic membrane model. Tumor immune-cell profiling was also performed to assess potential changes in major tumor-associated immune-cell populations. This dual-functional nanomedicine therefore provides an innovative therapeutic strategy that not only augments IRI efficacy but also confers metastasis suppression and favorable pharmacokinetics, addressing critical unmet needs in mCRC treatment. These findings highlight the translational potential of IRI@(SO3-)-MSN-PEG/TA as a safer and more effective therapeutic strategy for mCRC.

title: Multifunctional Mesoporous Bioactive Glass Nanoparticles Promote Osteogenesis via Immunomodulation
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous bioactive glass (MBG) is a promising biomaterial for bone-defect repair. However, MBG lacks an immunomodulatory capability, which is vital for effective bone regeneration, thus limiting its clinical application. Herein, MBG grafted with mannose (MBG-g-Man) was designed to target and interact with macrophages via the recognition of the mannose receptor (CD206) and promote M2 polarization. In vitro experiments demonstrated that MBG-g-Man exhibits excellent biocompatibility, precise macrophage targeting, and efficient cellular uptake while also recruiting and polarizing macrophages toward the M2 phenotype. Furthermore, osteogenic differentiation assays revealed that the ALP activity of MBG-g-Man was 157.89 units/L, which is much higher than that of MBG (127.85 units/L), demonstrating that MBG-g-Man may be an effective bone regeneration material. This research may provide a promising strategy for designing functional biomaterials for bone tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.

title: A Three-Dimensional Bimetallic Triazolate Metal–Organic Framework as a Conductive Electrode for High-Performance Solid-State Supercapacitors
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report the rational design of a three-dimensional ultramicroporous bimetallic triazolate framework, FeCo-(triz)2, constructed by integrating redox-active Fe and Co centers within a robust triazolate network. The synergistic electronic interaction between the Fe and Co nodes increases the density of accessible redox-active sites while facilitating rapid electron transport and enhanced charge-transfer kinetics. Simultaneously, the strong coordination between the triazolate ligands and bimetallic nodes imparts exceptional structural and chemical stability under electrochemical operating conditions. The interconnected ultramicroporous architecture, combined with multiple accessible Fe/Co oxidation states and intrinsic electrical conductivity, promotes efficient electrolyte infiltration and accelerated ion diffusion throughout the framework. As a result, the FeCo-(triz)2 electrode delivers a high specific capacitance of 926 F g–1 at a current density of 1 A g–1 and retains 57% of its capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 99% at 5 A g–1 after 3000 galvanostatic charge–discharge cycles. Furthermore, an all-solid-state asymmetric supercapacitor assembled using conducting additive-free FeCo-(triz)2 as the cathode exhibits a specific capacitance of 60 F g–1 at 1 A g–1, with an energy density of 8.6 Wh kg–1 at a power density of 7731 W kg–1, outperforming many previously reported MOF- and carbon-based electrodes. The device also demonstrates remarkable long-term durability, retaining 87.5% of its initial capacitance with a Coulombic efficiency of 98.33% after 10,000 charge–discharge cycles at 5 A g–1. These findings establish the bimetallic triazolate strategy as an effective approach for overcoming the intrinsic limitations of MOF electrodes and highlight FeCo-(triz)2 as a robust and efficient electrode material for next-generation solid-state energy-storage devices.

title: Surface‐Stabilized Sub‐Micron Condensates for Compartmentalizing Synthetic Cells and Enhanced Enzyme Kinetics
abstract: Living cells harbor numerous membraneless organelles (MOs), which are dynamic protein/nucleic acid assemblies responding to specific physicochemical triggers. Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) plays a crucial role in their formation and activity. Inspired by the natural MOs that maintain their individual identities, this work presents a bioengineering strategy to generate LLPS‐driven, isochemical MO populations using surfactant‐like peptides that stabilize the MO interface. The result is highly stable, monodispersed, sub‐µm‐sized MO populations, which are not only capable of compartmentalizing synthetic cells but also provide superior environments for enzymatic reactions. This is achieved using pH‐responsive elastin‐like polypeptides (PREs) as MOs and formulating an amphiphilic PRE‐based peptide to stabilize the MO interface. Relative abundance of the surface‐active peptide, as well as the rate of pH change, allows direct control over the MO size. Encapsulating these components within synthetic vesicles using a microfluidic platform leads to on‐demand multi‐compartmentalization via an external pH trigger. Lastly, a functional consequence of the acute size control is shown through a phosphatase reaction, where the highest reaction rate is observed in size‐controlled MOs when compared to dilute environments and surfactant‐free MOs. The presented strategy provides a new avenue for designing programmable MOs and thus achieve functional compartmentalization within synthetic cells.

title: Deterministic Porous Dielectrics Through Microfluidic Building‐Block Assembly for Enhanced Pressure Transduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous dielectrics offer an effective route to enhance electromechanical transduction in flexible capacitive sensors, yet their architectures are typically governed by stochastic pore‐forming processes, limiting control over structural and dielectric responses. Here, we develop a microfluidic building‐block assembly strategy for constructing deterministic MWCNT/MXene@PDMS porous dielectrics. Monodisperse composite microspheres are generated through microfluidic confinement and assembled into interconnected three‐dimensional networks, enabling systematic regulation of microsphere dimensions and porosity. Under compression, structural deformation is coupled with enhanced interfacial polarization and dynamic microcapacitive interactions between MWCNT/MXene nanofillers, collectively amplifying the pressure‐dependent dielectric response. The resulting sensor achieves a sensitivity of 0.1889 kPa −1 at 0–5 kPa, a detection limit of 3 Pa, and a working range up to 365 kPa, together with stable cyclic performance. Its reproducible electromechanical response further enables human‐motion and plantar‐pressure monitoring, machine‐learning‐assisted pressure‐pattern recognition, and Morse‐code‐based nonverbal communication. This work establishes microfluidic building‐block assembly as a route from stochastic pore formation to deterministic porous dielectrics, linking mesoscale structural control with dielectric modulation and functional pressure transduction.

title: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
abstract: Abstract Algal organic matter (AOM) has been considered a typical pollutant in algal bloom waters, conventionally managed through flocculation-flotation processes with high carbon footprints. This study presents a paradigm shift by redefining AOM as a functional crosslinker and developing an AOM-induced self-driven flotation (A-SDF) strategy. The approach utilizes active groups in AOM (-COOH/-OH) coordinated with trace amounts of metal coagulants to construct multilevel gel flocs with Al 2 O 3 /FeO(OH) crystalline phases. Remarkably, these flocs not only capture algal cells but also activate dissolved oxygen (DO), inducing DO enrichment-interfacial gas nucleation behavior (DOE-IGNB) and leading to microbubbles (MBs) formation at the floc interface under mild turbulence. The process achieved efficient removal of algal cells (82–95%), turbidity (86–95%), and AOM (45–79%) within 2 min without external aeration. Compared with existing technologies, the carbon footprint, treatment time, and economic cost were reduced by 66.08–96.90%, 71.67–96.00%, and 50.55–97.67%, respectively, while residual metal concentrations remained well below drinking water standards. Density functional theory calculations confirmed strong DO adsorption by tetrahedral AlO 4 /FeO 4 lattices as the molecular mechanism driving DOE-IGNB. By repurposing AOM as a resource and activating endogenous DO, this work provides a universal carbon-neutral pathway for sustainable algal bloom management worldwide.

title: Bimetallic MOF-based electrochemical sensors for detecting synthetic phenolic antioxidants: design strategies, workflow, and future directions
abstract: -butylhydroquinone (TBHQ), butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT), and propyl gallate (PG), are extensively utilized to prevent lipid rancidity in processed foods. However, growing toxicological concerns regarding their potential hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, and endocrine-disrupting hazards motivate the development of rapid and sensitive screening tools. Electrochemical sensors modified with bimetallic metal-organic frameworks (BMOFs) have emerged as attractive sensing platforms because of their atomic-level dual-metal coordination, tunable pore architectures, and abundant catalytic active sites. This review provides an evidence-based evaluation of BMOF-based electrochemical sensors for SPAs. We assess the literature against four criteria: (1) matched monometallic controls to separate bimetallic effects from conductive-additive contributions; (2) electrochemical evidence for the overall proton/electron stoichiometry and, where available, for the proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) pathway; (3) density functional theory (DFT) support for adsorption energetics and d-band modulation, where available; and (4) reported statistical comparison with chromatographic reference techniques (HPLC-DAD). By evaluating pristine BMOFs, conductive nanocomposites (rGO, CNTs, and MXenes), and BMOF-derived porous heterostructures against these criteria, this review identifies the gaps that must be closed to move laboratory proof-of-concept sensors toward regulatory-grade food-safety screening.

title: Geometry-driven confinement and iodine evolution in robust metal–organic frameworks for adsorptive iodine storage
abstract: Efficient volatile iodine uptake and release is crucial for nuclear waste remediation and aerospace propulsion. However, current sorbents often face a trade-off between high capacity and facile regeneration, as strong host–guest interactions can hinder low-energy iodine release. Here, we report a reticular chemistry strategy combining geometry-driven confinement and structural retrofitting to address this challenge. In MOF-521, favorable geometric matching between one-dimensional rhombic channels and I2 molecules promotes dense iodine confinement, achieving an intrapore packing density of 3.18 g·cm−3 and utilizing approximately 65% of the available pore space. Comprehensive investigations integrating single-crystal X-ray diffraction (SCXRD), three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED), powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD), Raman and XPS spectroscopy, electrical conductivity measurements, and theoretical calculations reveal a dual-stage synergistic capture mechanism. Initial iodine incorporation involves speciation evolution and charge redistribution, followed by progressive geometry-confined physical filling and dense iodine organization. SCXRD further resolves ordered iodine assemblies with short I···I contact, highlighting the role of spatial confinement in promoting dense packing. However, such confined packing also contributes to framework deformation during desorption. Replacing monodentate formate with ditopic fumarate yields MOF-521-Fum with a distinct wwq topology. This structural retrofit maintains a high intrapore packing density of 2.79 g·cm−3, raises the decomposition temperature by 200 °C, enables complete iodine desorption, and achieves 96% capacity retention after four cycles. These findings highlight geometry-driven confinement and targeted structural regulation as complementary strategies for balancing dense iodine storage and reversible release.

title: A Low-Rank Modeling Framework for Adsorption Isotherm Reconstruction in Metal–Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Adsorptive separation offers an energy-efficient alternative to distillation, yet adsorption data sets often remain incomplete due to the high cost of experiments and simulations, limiting their use in large-scale materials screening. In this work, we address the challenge of sparsity in adsorption data sets by reformulating adsorption isotherms as an incomplete material–adsorption property matrix and analyzing them using a low-rank modeling (LRM) framework. Using Ar and N2 adsorption in metal–organic frameworks as representative case studies, we demonstrate that adsorption properties across pressures and adsorbates exhibit strong and systematic correlations, revealing an inherent low-rank structure in the adsorption data. Our analysis shows that reconstruction performance depends on the latent dimension (k) and regularization strength (λ), with the optimal ranges of k and λ determined from systematic hyperparameter analysis. Comparison of different LRM variants demonstrates that latent representations are important for capturing pressure-dependent trends, with the latent-bias (LB) and latent-only (LO) models consistently providing substantially better reconstruction than the bias-only (BO) model in the considered reconstruction settings. The LRM framework captures both the qualitative shape of adsorption isotherms and the absolute magnitude of uptake across a wide range of materials and adsorption behaviors. Systematic variation of data availability shows that reconstruction accuracy improves with increasing availability of observed entries, while naturally occurring pressure-dependent missingness in the N2 data set can also be reconstructed without requiring additional simulations. Cross-adsorbate analysis further shows that Ar adsorption contains information that can be used to reconstruct N2 adsorption, while jointly available Ar–N2 data substantially improve the performance of latent models. Quantitative comparison with the Uni-MOF framework shows that the latent LRM models achieve comparable or higher R2 values at several corresponding pressure points for Ar and N2 adsorption. Overall, these results demonstrate that LRM offers a data-efficient approach for reconstructing adsorption isotherms from incomplete data sets by leveraging correlations within adsorption properties.

title: Harnessing Weak Intermolecular Interactions for Efficient PFOA Capture in a Fluorine-Rich Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework Membrane
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic framework (3D-COF) membranes with open porosity represent a promising class of next-generation materials, particularly for selective molecular separations. In this work, we synthesized a fluorinated 3D-COF membrane (Tam-Tfta) via a liquid–liquid interfacial polymerization reaction for the efficient removal of perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). Owing to the abundance of fluorine functional groups within the COF backbone, the membrane achieved quantitative sequestration of PFOA from wastewater at environmentally relevant concentrations (1.0 μg L–1), while maintaining a high water permeance of ∼40 L m–2 h–1 bar–1. Mechanistic analysis reveals that the 3D-COF membrane enables favorable, orientation-assisted interactions within its pores, facilitating effective capture of amphiphilic PFOA molecules in contaminated water. This work represents one of the first demonstrations of a pure 3D COF membrane specifically engineered for removing PFAS.

title: Recent Advances in Mesoporous Catalysts for Polyolefin Upcycling
abstract: Abstract Polyolefins account for the largest fraction of global plastic production, yet traditional disposal methods like landfilling and incineration cause severe pollution and resource waste. Chemical upcycling offers a promising route to transform waste polyolefins into value-added products; however, the efficient conversion of bulky polymer chains remains challenging due to mass-transfer limitations and restricted control over catalytic environments. Characterized by high specific surface areas, large pore sizes, tunable pore structures, and easily functionalized surfaces, mesoporous materials offer unique opportunities for addressing these challenges. This outlook systematically reviews the recent advances in mesoporous catalysts for four prevalent polyolefin upcycling strategies: catalytic cracking/hydrocracking, hydrogenolysis, selective oxidation, and emerging tandem/coupling technologies. We specifically summarize the critical bottlenecks of each process and highlight the pivotal roles of mesoporous catalysts in overcoming these limitations. Furthermore, the structure–activity relationships of these catalysts are discussed, followed by insights into the future design of advanced mesoporous catalytic systems.

title: Catalytic performance of hierarchically porous catalysts with various distributions of micropores and mesopores during pyrolysis of oleic acid
abstract: Abstract Non-edible lipids are a significant source of renewable liquid biofuels to mitigate CO2 emissions, especially for production of sustainable aviation fuels. The pathway of catalytic pyrolysis can convert lipids to sustainable liquid biofuels under mild reaction conditions without H2 consumption. However, it is hindered by quick deactivation of catalysts due to coking and inflexible selectivity of liquid product fractions. In this study, hierarchically porous zeolites were developed via the alkaline treatment and template methods. The relationship between the composition of liquid biofuels and the distribution of micropores and mesopores in hierarchically porous catalysts was discussed emphatically. The comprehensive characterization of catalysts confirmed the hierarchically porous structure with different volume ratios of micropore and mesopore (1:0.18–1:4) and average pore size distribution (1.99–6.24 nm). Composition of liquid biofuels obtained from catalytic pyrolysis with these hierarchically porous catalysts was also analyzed. A high kerosene selectivity (more than 40% for C10–C14) was obtained for the hierarchically porous catalyst SA-ZM-0.5 with a volume ratio (1:0.39) of micropore and mesopore during catalytic pyrolysis of oleic acid. For the catalyst series with different pore size distribution, the catalyst SB-ZM-II exhibited 79.87% selectivity for C5–C9 fractions with the maximum specific surface area (724 m2∙g-1) and the maximum mesoporous volume (0.90 cm3·g-1). The catalytic pyrolysis for conversion of non-edible lipids into liquid hydrocarbons involves a series of reactions such as cracking, deoxygenation, and carbon chain modification through aromatization and isomerization, which need deep research with simulation and model compounds.

title: Fabrication of Large-Pore Volume Phosphorus-Doped Porous Carbon Spheres Derived from tert -Butyl Alcohol and Formaldehyde for the Removal of Rhodamine B
abstract: Hierarchical carbon materials containing both bimodal mesoporous and macroporous structures have enhanced properties with controlled morphology. In this paper, phosphorus-doped porous carbon microspheres (PMCSs) derived from the carbon deposition reaction were obtained by a novel and feasible template approach at a low temperature range of 300–500 °C, with tert-butyl alcohol and formaldehyde as carbon sources and P-impregnated commercial silica gel as the template, catalyst, and phosphorus source. More importantly, the obtained PMCSs with spherical morphology possess abundant mesopores, high specific surface areas (692 m2g–1), and ultrahollow carbon frameworks (5.83 cm3g–1), as well as phosphorus doping (0.34 wt %) in the carbon matrix. Due to these merits, PMCSs were investigated as adsorbents for the removal of Rhodamine B (RhB) and exhibited excellent adsorption performance (313 mg/g), which is higher than those reported in most previous studies. The current work provides new insights into the rational design of heteroatom-doped porous carbonaceous materials and shows that carbon deposition has the potential to be an effective, low-cost, and scalable route toward the preparation of promising high-performance hierarchical carbon materials in the future.

title: Functionalised biocompatible and biodegradable amphiphilic block copolymer particles produced by self-assembly and electrospraying for biomedical applications
abstract: The work presented in this thesis focuses on the preparation of biocompatible and biodegradable amphiphilic block copolymer nanostructures suitable for biomedical applications. These polymers were prepared using a combination of reversible addition fragmentation chain-transfer (RAFT) polymerisation and ring opening polymerisation (ROP). These methods were combined in a simultaneous process under bulk conditions. Functional monomers were used to incorporate various properties into polymer chains, and particles were formed using self-assembly and electrospraying techniques. Chapter 1 describes the ROP and RAFT polymerisation processes and the suitability of these polymer materials in a biomedical setting, including the delivery of cancer treatments and gene therapy. Chapter 2 covers the synthesis of a variety of amphiphilic block copolymers through the combined ROP-RAFT polymerisation process. This was achieved using a bifunctional ROP-RAFT agent containing an -OH group capable of acting as a ROP initiator. Amphiphilic block copolymers contained either poly(trimethylene carbonate) (PTMC) or poly(lactide) (PLA) as a biodegradable hydrophobic block prepared via ROP. A range of monomers were used to synthesise the hydrophilic block via RAFT polymerisation, including biocompatible oligo(ethylene glycol methyl ether methacrylate) (OEGMA) or 2-methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine (MPC), cationic 2-(dimethylamino)ethyl methacrylate (DMAEMA) for DNA complexation, and functional monomers 4-formylphenyl methacrylate (FPMA) or methacrylic acid N-hydroxysuccinimide ester (NHSMA) for conjugation of biomolecules. In Chapter 3 a set of these polymers were selected for the preparation of nanoparticles by selfassembly. Solvent switch and thin film rehydration techniques were assessed, and the resultant morphologies were found to form mainly vesicle structures. Vesicles containing DMAEMA were tested for their ability to form complexes with DNA, as well as their cytotoxicity. Polymers containing NHSMA or FPMA groups were used to attach fluorescent dyes or RGD peptide to the vesicle surface. Blends of copolymers were examined for their cytotoxicity and stability in a serum environment. Chapter 4 covers the formation of PTMC-based amphiphilic block copolymer particles by electrospraying. A range of electrospraying conditions were investigated, including polymer concentration, solvent and flow rate of PTMC-b-POEGMA block copolymers, and blends with added PTMC homopolymer. Some of these polymers also contained NHSMA or FPMA functional groups for the potential of conjugating biomolecules to the particle surface. Finally, the thesis conclusions and future work are presented in Chapter 5.

title: Minimal metabolite assembly kinetics revealing a novel role for chaperones
abstract: Inborn errors of metabolism lead to the toxic accumulation of metabolites, a process that is associated with the onset of severe disorders like Phenylketonuria or Gaucher disease. Numerous studies have shown that these metabolites can form amyloid-like assemblies upon accumulation. Yet the mechanisms underlying their self-assembly and cellular regulation remain unclear. Here we show that three disease-associated metabolites, adenine, glucosylceramide and phenylalanine, self-assemble through different non-canonical pathways, including polymorphic restructuring, clustering and concentration-dependent pathway switching. Minimal phenomenological kinetic models quantitatively captured these behaviours across broad concentration ranges, providing a unified framework for metabolite self-assembly. Through interactome analyses of cellular lysates we identified multiple molecular chaperones associated with metabolite assemblies. Kinetics analysis of selected chaperones revealed that they target specific assembly steps such as nucleation, elongation, and remodelling the assembly pathways. These findings demonstrate molecular chaperones as modulators of metabolite aggregation and extend their role beyond classic proteostasis towards metabolostasis.

title: Controlled Self-Assembly of Homointerlocked [2]Catenanes Containing Two Discrete Cages via Coordination and Noncovalent Interactions
abstract: Abstract Triply interlocked systems constitute a sophisticated class of topological architectures in which two discrete coordination cages are mechanically interlocked. The controlled and straightforward construction of such aesthetically appealing structures remains a longstanding synthetic challenge. Herein, we report the efficient assembly of two homointerlocked [2]catenanes cntaining two identical monomeric cages, via a coordination-driven self-assembly strategy that integrates half-sandwich metal units with judiciously designed tridentate ligands and exploits synergistic noncovalent interactions. The formation and structural features of these triply interlocked systems were unambiguously established by 1H NMR spectroscopy and single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Notably, when the same binuclear organometallic building block was employed, replacement of the tridentate bridging ligand with a nonplanar tetradentate analogue completely suppressed formation of the interlocked architecture, underscoring the critical role of ligand geometry in directing the self-assembly of complex molecular topologies.

title: Promoting 5-Hydroxytryptophan Production via Hydrophobic Short Peptide-Driven Self-Assembly of Key Enzymes
abstract: An optimization strategy using self-assembling peptides (SAPs) was developed to enhance the biosynthesis of 5-hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP). Tryptophan hydroxylase (TPH2H318E/H323E) was fused with three distinct SAPs (EAK16, ELK16, and L6KD) via a flexible linker to promote the in situ formation of active protein aggregates (APAs). Among the candidates, the hydrophobic ELK16 peptide demonstrated the most superior performance, achieving a self-assembly efficiency of 98.0%, a recovery yield of 94.8%, and a final purity of 95% via simple centrifugation, without any chromatographic step. Compared to the free enzyme, the TPH2H318E/H323E-ELK16 aggregates exhibited significantly broader thermal tolerance, shifting the optimal temperature upward by 2 °C and extending the thermal inactivation half-life (t1/2) at 40 °C from 31.6 h to 37.5 h (1.2-fold). The aggregates also maintained high catalytic activity across a wider pH range (6.5–9.0). In an eight-channel pH-controlled reactor, the ELK16-induced aggregate system reached a substrate conversion rate of 95.2% within 12 h, yielding 10.48 g·L−1 of 5-HTP with no detectable residual substrate. Furthermore, the insoluble aggregates retained more than 72.6% of their initial catalytic activity after five consecutive reuse cycles. This strategy provides an efficient, recyclable biocatalyst platform for cost-effective green biomanufacturing.

title: Catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation for precise synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes
abstract: Organic semiconductors such as polythiophenes (PThs) offer substantial potential for flexible optoelectronics. Incorporating silicon into the PTh backbone represents a promising strategy to enhance flexibility and tune electronic properties; however, conventional metal-catalyzed synthetic approaches lack precise control over polymer chain growth, yielding materials with poorly defined energy levels and relatively board dispersity. Here, we report a catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation (TDP) strategy for the direct incorporation of silicon into PThs, producing a class of narrowly dispersed silicon-incorporated polymers. This thermally driven, radical-mediated mechanism circumvents the uncontrolled initiation and competitive pathways of conventional catalytic routes, enabling precise control over chain growth and yielding well-defined PThs with narrow dispersity ( Đ = 1.2 – 1.4). The dehydrogenatively coupled diphenylsilane- terthiophene polymer (PS-1) shows favorable energy-level alignment and a hole mobility of 9.2 × 10 −4 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . When employed as a hole-transport interlayer in inverted tin-lead (Sn-Pb) perovskite solar cells, PS-1 enables a champion power conversion efficiency of 23.3% with enhanced operational stability, surpassing the 20.8% efficiency of standard PEDOT:PSS-based devices. This work establishes a scalable synthetic route to advanced conjugated polymers, providing a versatile materials platform for optoelectronic applications.

title: Three-dimensional structural engineering of Zn anodes for advanced aqueous zinc-ion batteries: mechanisms, challenges, and prospects
abstract: Benefiting from their intrinsic safety, earth-abundant zinc resources, low manufacturing cost, and environmentally benign chemistry, aqueous zinc-based batteries have emerged as a compelling candidate for next-generation sustainable energy storage systems. Although metallic Zn anodes offer a high theoretical capacity and an advantageous redox potential, their practical application is severely hindered by interfacial instability issues, including dendritic growth, dead-Zn formation, hydrogen evolution, and corrosion, leading to poor Coulombic efficiency and limited cycling durability. While extensive research has focused on material-level optimization, the translation of lab-scale advances into commercially viable devices hinges on scalable and controllable manufacturing technologies. In this review, we address this gap by presenting a manufacturing-centric analysis of three-dimensional (3D) Zn anode engineering. We systematically evaluate how advanced manufacturing processes, including additive manufacturing, laser ablation, electrospinning, template imprinting, and electrodeposition, enable precise regulation of electrode architecture, local electric fields, and Zn 2+ transport pathways. These advantages collectively promote uniform Zn plating/stripping, suppress dendrite growth, and alleviate parasitic side reactions. This review provides a systematic overview of recent progress in topology-guided 3D Zn anodes, encompassing representative fabrication strategies. Furthermore, structure‒performance relationships across various 3D designs have been elucidated. Finally, we outline the remaining challenges and future research directions toward durable, scalable, and high-performance zinc-based energy storage.

title: Conformation Preorganization of Hydrogen-Bonded Foldamers for Hierarchical Halogen-Bond-Driven Supramolecular Self-assembly
abstract: Halogen bonding, featured by high strength and outstanding directionality, has become a powerful driving force for fabricating such supramolecular architectures. Herein, we report a two component supramolecular co crystal assembled from hydrogen bonded foldamers and halogen bond donors. Benefiting from intramolecular three center hydrogen bonds, compound 1 maintains a typical crescent conformation, whereas compound 3 exhibits subtle distortion at its pyridyl terminus caused by weakened local hydrogen bonding. Such distortion promotes π π stacking and yields linearly arranged compound 3 as key linear structural units. The distorted pyridyl termini bind compound 1 through intermolecular hydrogen bonds, and compound 1 further forms cyclic dimeric motifs driven by dual intermolecular halogen bonds. Linear and cyclic motifs cross link cooperatively to realize stepwise hierarchical assembly toward two dimensional supramolecular networks. Single-crystal analysis reveals that compound 2 adopts a meniscus-shaped conformation locked by two sets of intramolecular three-center hydrogen bonds and assembles into macrocycles via intermolecular halogen-bond-mediated dimerization. This work demonstrates how subtle conformational differences of foldamers modulate aggregate topology via multiple noncovalent synergy, offering a feasible strategy for controllable construction of foldamer based high order supramolecular networks.

abstract: By investigating the chemical and electrochemical behavior of iron trihalides, which are promising low-cost, earth-abundant intercalation materials, we reveal that superconcentrated electrolytes drive the self-assembly of new coordination compounds that crystallize via a solvent-exchange mechanism.
